claims.text: Adding a sintering aid to a powder mixture can reduce the required sintering temperature.
A sintering aid can induce a transient liquid phase during sintering.
The transient liquid phase promotes mass transport and densification.
The proposed starting material is a powder mixture of ceramic or similar inorganic materials intended for sintering.
The intervention is to introduce a controlled amount of a liquid-phase-promoting sintering aid into the powder mixture.
A transient liquid phase forms at particle boundaries during sintering.
The liquid phase lowers the energy barrier for mass transfer between particles.
Enhanced mass transfer facilitates densification at a lower temperature than conventional solid-state sintering.
A sample containing the sintering aid will attain similar or improved densification at a lower temperature than an additive-free sample.
Standard solid-state sintering without an aid generally requires higher temperatures to attain similar densification.
The method is applicable only when the sintering aid does not compromise final material properties.
The method requires formation of a beneficial liquid phase without detrimental side reactions.
No eligible evidence was provided to directly support the proposed method or mechanism in a particular material system.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant densification improvement at a lower temperature relative to the additive-free control would falsify the hypothesis.
An adverse effect of the additive on final material properties would falsify the hypothesis.
